title: Code Review Findings
description: What each reviewer subagent writes to its artifact file. The compact return is a subset of this.

reviewer.description: Reviewer identifier; matches the artifact filename stem. One of protection-warrior, subtlety-rogue, havoc-demon-hunter, marksmanship-hunter, fire-mage, restoration-shaman, retribution-paladin, unholy-death-knight, balance-druid, demonology-warlock, windwalker-monk, lore-bard, augmentation-evoker, discipline-priest, the orchestrator's fast-pass, or havoc-demon-hunter-peer for the cross-model pass.

model.description: Set only by the cross-model peer: the model that served the review, as the peer CLI reported it.

independence_verified.description: Set only by the cross-model peer: true when the serving model belongs to a different family than the host session. Only a true value lets peer agreement raise another reviewer's confidence.

findings.description: Each finding this persona will stand behind at confidence 50 or above. Empty when there are none.

title.description: The symptom, ten words or fewer.

severity.description: P0 must fix before merge. P1 should fix. P2 fix if straightforward. P3 discretionary.

file.description: Path relative to the repo root.

line.description: The line the finding points at. A wrong line is worse than no finding.

why_it_matters.description: What breaks and for whom, effect first, then why the fix resolves it. Two to four sentences. Never empty.

autofix_class.description: Shape of the follow-up; the reviewer applies nothing. gated_auto: a concrete suggested_fix exists and can be applied after a judgment call. manual: fixable but needs a design or cross-cutting decision. advisory: report only.

owner.description: Who acts next. downstream-resolver for anything fixable in code. human only when a product decision, missing authority, or outside coordination blocks it. release for rollout actions.

requires_verification.description: True when the fix should not be trusted without targeted tests or a follow-up check.

suggested_fix.description: The concrete change you would make if you had to choose now, with any assumption named. Name the specific guard or call, never 'add validation'. Null only when no code-level change exists to propose: a pure question, or an organizational resolution. Withholding a fix because information is incomplete is the failure this field exists to prevent.

confidence.description: One of five anchors, each tied to work you did. 0: does not hold up, or not introduced by this diff. 25: possibly real, unverified. Neither of those is emitted. 50: verified, but a nit, a narrow edge, or low impact; style lives here. 75: checked the diff and surrounding code and can name the observable consequence in normal use. 100: provable from the code alone (compile or type error, definitive logic bug, quotable standards violation).

evidence.description: Code-grounded proof: quoted lines with file:line, or pattern descriptions. At 75 or 100 the first item must be the verbatim line that makes the finding true; if you cannot quote it, drop to 50. When history carries the claim (pre_existing, intentional design, introduced by this diff, or P0/P1 severity that depends on age), append one provenance line from a targeted git blame or log: short sha, author, date, subject. Provenance never replaces the quoted line and is omitted when the diff alone justifies the finding.

pre_existing.description: True only for unchanged code the diff neither touches nor makes newly reachable.

requirement.description: The requirement id from the <requirements> block (R1, R2) this finding shows unmet, or null.

residual_risks.description: Concerns you could not raise to a finding, including coverage limits of your own search.

testing_gaps.description: Scenarios the change should have tests for and does not.
